description: Classification of product, donor and legacy identity in tracked files (N0.1), and the independence gate (N0.9). Rules are ordered: the first rule whose path, term and line patterns all match classifies a finding. Every rule has a reason; every rule but the last has at least one constraint. The census tool, this policy, its test and the census artifact are not scanned: they must name every term.

categories.ACTIVE_PRODUCT_IDENTITY: Product-facing name or copy; changes to Ninerr.
categories.ACTIVE_INTERNAL_IDENTITY: Internal identifier, comment or donor attribution in active code; changes or is removed.
categories.PUBLIC_API: Identifier a user, agent or integration addresses; migrates with a transition path.
categories.PERSISTED_DATA: Identity written to disk; needs a versioned migration and a legacy reader.
categories.LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY: Recognizes legacy identity so existing data keeps working; transitional, never written for new data.
categories.TEST_FIXTURE: Test or fixture content; updates with the code it tests.
categories.THIRD_PARTY_INDEPENDENT_OBLIGATION: Names an independently licensed dependency or runtime whose license obligations Ninerr keeps.
categories.IMMUTABLE_HISTORICAL_FACT: A dated record of what happened; not rewritten.
categories.REMOVE_ENTIRELY: Retired material with no role in Ninerr; removed from the tree (history keeps it).

rules.reason: Paper artifact recovery tooling; no role in Ninerr (N0-G5).
Paper artifact recovery records; Git history preserves them (N0-G5).
Dated qualification records (date-suffixed) describe the product as it was named when they were written.
Golden projects in the legacy format: the migration corpus that proves old projects still open.
License notices and register entries for independently licensed runtimes Ninerr keeps; donor entries in the same files stay gated until N0-G5 and N0-G7 resolve them.
Impeccable is an independently licensed (Apache-2.0) runtime dependency invoked as a separate process.
Docling is an optional, independently licensed local runtime that the import stack invokes; it is never distributed.
Project directory, manifest format and journal genesis domain written into every project (N0-G2).
Registries, discovery file, credential prefix and projects-folder default written to the user's disk (N0-G2).
History tool identifiers recorded in every journal entry (N0-G3).
Environment variables users and MCP clients set (N0-G3, legacy names read with a notice).
MCP tool catalog mirrored from Paper and checked for drift against it (N0-G4).
Commands and entry points users run (N0-G3).
Per-package donor attribution and donor ledgers; consolidated into one provenance register (N0-G5).
Tests and fixtures move with the code they test.
Any other Lilac occurrence is active identity.
Any other Paper occurrence is donor product identity.
Any other donor name in active material.
